html:
Kenya is a country in East Africa on the Indian Ocean, with Nairobi as its capital. Britain ruled it from 1895, as a colony from 1920, until independence in 1963.

The coast had a much older history as part of the Swahili city-states. Mombasa traded across the Indian Ocean, and the Portuguese built Fort Jesus there in 1593.

Britain built the Uganda Railway inland from Mombasa from 1896, and Nairobi grew up as a railway camp. White settlers took the cool, fertile "White Highlands", pushing out Kikuyu and Maasai.

  • 1952 to 1960: the Mau Mau rebellion. Britain declared an emergency and held tens of thousands in detention camps.
  • 1963: independence, with Jomo Kenyatta as leader.
  • 1978 to 2002: Daniel arap Moi, who ran a one-party state until 1991.
  • 2007 to 2008: violence after a disputed election killed over a thousand people.

The writer Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o and the tree planter Wangari Maathai are among its best-known figures.
sum: Kenya is a country in East Africa on the Indian Ocean, with Nairobi as its capital. Britain ruled it from 1895, as a colony from 1920, until independence in 1963.
